items.risk: Q3 cost of sales included an $82M tariff-refund benefit, so reported margin expansion should not be treated as entirely recurring.
Raised expectations increase the future delivery bar; geopolitical and regional demand conditions remain variable.
Integrated breadth can improve cross-division leverage but does not itself establish control of an irreplaceable bottleneck; customers can retain heterogeneous automation and software stacks.

Successor bottlenecks may migrate from control hardware/software toward electricity availability, interconnection, skilled labor, cybersecurity and customer data quality, limiting how much value Emerson can capture.
Adjusted profitability can overstate recurring economics if tariff refunds, restructuring exclusions or acquisition-related amortization are treated as normal operating improvement.
Acquisition-led portfolio expansion creates integration and capital-allocation exposure; AI/software capabilities face rapid competitive response and substitution.
Geographic and end-market variability plus tariffs/currency/geopolitical conditions can interrupt an otherwise constructive demand cycle.

contradictions.contradiction: Strong adjusted Test & Measurement margin coexists with much lower GAAP EBIT margin, so profitability quality depends materially on treatment of amortization and restructuring.
contradictions.resolution: Treat adjusted margin as an operating lens, not equivalent to GAAP economic earnings; retain acquisition-related costs as a present risk rather than a blocker.

unknowns.unknown: Current sources do not establish security-level valuation attractiveness or isolate long-run pricing power from mix and inflation recovery.
Current evidence does not quantify customer switching costs or prove that AVA/AspenTech integration materially raises retention versus competing interoperable stacks.
Current evidence does not establish whether recent AI acquisitions will generate incremental organic revenue sufficient to exceed integration and acquisition costs.
No evidence reviewed here proves durable pricing power independent of mix, inflation recovery and the current infrastructure demand cycle.
